standard_prerequisites.name: A finite module over a Noetherian ring admits a resolution by finite free modules, and the set of primes at which the module is free is open
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the resolution whose syzygies are studied and makes the loci U_i open subsets of the spectrum.

standard_prerequisites.name: A finite projective module over a local ring is free, and a finitely generated module of finite projective dimension at a prime can be replaced by a free one after passing to a large syzygy
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the loci U_i are increasing and that a large syzygy is free at every prime, hence projective.

standard_prerequisites.name: The spectrum of a Noetherian ring is a Noetherian topological space, so an increasing sequence of open subsets that covers it stabilizes, and for a bounded complex with finite cohomology each cohomology module is perfect
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the finite index n at which the covering stabilizes and reduces part (2) to part (1) applied to the cohomology modules.

core_obligations: For part (1), note that a perfect module is finite by definition, and conversely let M be finite and choose a resolution by finite free modules, writing M_i for the successive kernels (proof lines 19125-19132).

Let U_i be the open set of primes at which M_i is free, show that p in U_i implies the sequence splits at p so that M_{i+1, p} is finite projective and hence free, and conclude that the U_i form an increasing sequence of opens (proof lines 19132-19141).

Show that the U_i cover the spectrum: at a prime p the local ring is regular, hence of finite global dimension, so a sufficiently large syzygy is finite projective and therefore free at p; since the spectrum is Noetherian, U_n is everything for some n (proof lines 19142-19152).
Conclude part (1): M_n is then projective, so the truncated resolution is a bounded resolution of M by finite projective modules and M is perfect (proof lines 19152-19161).

Conclude part (2): if K is perfect then it is bounded with finite cohomology by definition, while conversely a bounded complex with finite cohomology has each cohomology module perfect by part (1), whence the complex is perfect by the earlier criterion (proof lines 19163-19172).
proof_roadmap: Reduce part (1) to the study of the syzygies of a finite module along a finite free resolution (proof lines 19125-19132).
Show that the loci of primes where a syzygy is free are increasing opens, using that finite projective modules over local rings are free (proof lines 19132-19141).

Cover the spectrum by those loci through the finite global dimension of the regular local rings and Noetherianity of the spectrum, and read off that a large syzygy is projective (proof lines 19142-19161).
Deduce part (2) from part (1) and the criterion identifying perfect complexes with those whose cohomology modules are perfect (proof lines 19163-19172).
difficulty_reason: The statement characterizes perfect objects over a regular ring in two forms: a module is perfect exactly when it is finite, and a complex is perfect exactly when it is bounded with finite cohomology (statement lines 19114-19122). The proof of the first part is a covering argument: taking a finite free resolution of a finite module, the loci where the successive syzygies are free form an increasing sequence of opens because projectivity over a local ring is freeness, the local rings being regular have finite global dimension so a large syzygy is free at each prime, and Noetherianity of the spectrum makes the cover stabilize at some finite stage, after which the truncated resolution exhibits the module as perfect (proof lines 19124-19161). The second part is then deduced from the first by applying it to each cohomology module of a bounded complex.
